epic_id.description: The epic's identity (identifiers.adoc, epic_id); unchanged when the directory is archived with a dated suffix.

sources.description: What the epic started from, so that the ledger says it on every machine: per source of the epic's source directory its id, kind, reference, and digest, as its manifest records them (filesystem-layout/03, The Source Directory); written once by the epic's creation.

reference.description: An issue's or a pull request's URL, a lesson_id, a document's name; null for a description and the local changes.

intent.description: The epic's intent (model-work/08, Epic Intent): null until the first decomposition the operator agreed writes it; afterwards changed only by a decomposition the operator agreed.

parallelization_scope.description: The upper limit of the epic's running plans (a pausing or paused plan counting like a running one); taken from the project's epic.parallelization_scope at creation (its default: store-schemas/08, Operator Local Configuration, settings epic), raised only by the operator.

auto_start.description: The epic's mode: true, epic.next-work starts every launchable row up to parallelization_scope; false, it starts nothing by itself and reports each row that became launchable, and the operator's Next plan starts one. Taken from the project's epic.auto_start at creation (its default: store-schemas/08, settings epic).

overlap_max_files.description: How many files a launchable row's declared surface may share with a running plan's declared surface and realized changes before the row waits for that plan (wait reason overlap); taken from the project's epic.overlap_max_files at creation (its default and compiled upper bound: store-schemas/08, settings epic).

lifecycle.description: decomposing from creation; set to active by the transaction that writes the first decomposition the operator agreed (at least one staged row); set to terminal by epic.archive (epic.archive-ledger), together with terminal_reason and archived_at.

terminal_reason.description: Set iff lifecycle == terminal, by epic.archive: completed when the operator's archive passed its archive check, cancelled when the operator's cancel, the cancel of an integrity hold included, ended the epic (the reason text goes to the audit log, never into the header). The release of the project never writes the ledger: a released epic keeps its header as it was, and its terminal_reason released is recorded in the machine store only (store-schemas/02, terminal_reason).

archived_at.description: The epic's archive flag: set by epic.archive in the transaction that moves the directory to .marshall/archived-epics/; while it is set, epic.next-work starts and serves nothing.
